title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility — Account Adjustment Reasons
content:
**Adjustment code policy.** Besides QMB protection and hardship, three adjustments exist on Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility accounts. Each clause below names the adjustment reason under which it is posted.

## A. Prompt-pay discount

A prompt-pay discount of the class's prompt-pay percentage of a charge applies when the class offers one and the patient pays the charge in full no later than the class's prompt-pay window in calendar days after the first statement showing it; it is posted with the reason "prompt-pay discount" on the paying day and the payment due is reduced by it. *Partly retired:* for a prompt-pay discount on a coinsurance charge, and only for such a discount, this clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis; a prompt-pay discount on any other charge remains under this clause as written.

## B. Missing-notice write-off

A charge of the non-covered-with-notice or upgrade-difference type whose equipment record shows no signed notice on file before delivery is removed in full, with the reason "missing-notice write-off", when the class makes the supplier liable for a missing notice.

## C. Small-balance write-off

After the final statement cycle, an account balance of no more than the class's small-balance write-off ceiling is written off with the reason "small-balance write-off".

## D. Claim reversal

When an equipment or supply category reverses a paid claim line, every open charge stemming from that line is removed in full with the reason "claim reversal", on the reversal date.

## E. Stacking

Adjustments on one charge never stack beyond its open amount: when a hardship discount and a prompt-pay discount could both apply to the same charge, only the larger one is posted, and QMB protection displaces both. *Partly retired:* for a hardship discount or a prompt-pay discount, and only for those two discounts, the cap at the charge's open amount is no longer in force. Every other adjustment remains under this clause and never stacks beyond its charge's open amount; and when a hardship and a prompt-pay discount could both apply to one charge, only the larger is posted, with QMB protection displacing both.

## Points of judgement (clauses B to D)

| Fact on record | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Upgrade-difference charge; equipment record shows a notice signed before delivery | clause B does not remove it |
| Upgrade-difference charge; no signed notice on file before delivery; class makes the supplier liable | removed in full as missing-notice write-off |
| Balance of 4.99 after the final statement cycle (ceiling 4.99 in every class) | written off as small-balance write-off |
| Balance of 5.00 after the final statement cycle | above the ceiling; clause C does not write it off |
| Paid line reversed by its equipment category; two open charges stem from it | both removed in full as claim reversal on the reversal date |

superseded_clauses: Adjustments on one charge never stack beyond its open amount: when a hardship discount and a prompt-pay discount could both apply to the same charge, only the larger one is posted, and QMB protection displaces both.

A prompt-pay discount of `prompt_pay_discount_pct` of a charge applies when the class offers one and the patient pays the charge in full no later than `prompt_pay_window_days` calendar days after the first statement showing it; it is posted with adjustment_reason prompt_pay_discount on the paying day and the payment due is reduced by it.
